title: Minimax signal detection and separation rates

items.title: Weighted chi-square triangular-array limit
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. For each $n$, let $G_{n,1},\ldots,G_{n,m_n}$ be independent standard normal random variables, and let $w_{n,j}\ge0$ satisfy $2\sum_{j=1}^{m_n}w_{n,j}^2=1$. If $\max_{1\le j\le m_n}w_{n,j}\to0$, then $$T_n=\sum_{j=1}^{m_n}w_{n,j}(G_{n,j}^2-1)$$ has mean zero and variance one for every $n$ and converges in distribution to $N(0,1)$.

references.title: Yuri I. Ingster, Theofanis Sapatinas and Irina A. Suslina, Minimax signal detection in ill-posed inverse problems
Evarist Giné and Richard Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models

items.axiom_use: The Axiom of Choice is used only through the published Lindeberg–Feller theorem. The finite row-moment and Lindeberg estimates are choice-free.

items.title: Minimax detection risk and separation rate
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice and use the Gaussian sequence inverse model with singular values $s_j>0$, inverse-noise weights $\sigma_j=s_j^{-1}$, and parameter coordinates $\theta=(\theta_j)\in\ell^2$. Let $a=(a_j)$ be a positive nondecreasing sequence with $a_j\to\infty$, and let $\sigma=(\sigma_j)$ be a positive nondecreasing sequence with $\sigma_j\to\infty$. For $\varepsilon>0$, put $\eta_j=\theta_j/\sigma_j$ and observe $Y_j=Z_j/\sigma_j=\eta_j+\varepsilon\xi_j$, where $Z$ is the normalized observation in the Gaussian sequence inverse model and the $\xi_j$ are independent standard normal random variables. For $0<q\le2$ and $r>0$, define $$\Theta_q(r)=\left\{\eta\in\mathbb R^{\mathbb N}:(\sigma_j\eta_j)_{j\ge1}\in\ell^2,\ \sum_{j=1}^{\infty}|a_j\sigma_j\eta_j|^q\le1,\ \sum_{j=1}^{\infty}\sigma_j^2\eta_j^2\ge r^2\right\}.$$ Test $H_0:\eta=0$ against $H_1:\eta\in\Theta_q(r)$ by a product-Borel measurable randomized test $\psi:\mathbb R^{\mathbb N}\to[0,1]$, where $\psi(y)$ is the rejection probability. Its type-I error and maximal type-II error are $$\alpha_\varepsilon(\psi)=\mathbb E_{\varepsilon,0}\psi,\qquad \beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r),\psi)=\sup_{\eta\in\Theta_q(r)}\mathbb E_{\varepsilon,\eta}(1-\psi).$$ When $\Theta_q(r)=\varnothing$, define $\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r),\psi)=\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r),\alpha)=\gamma_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r))=0$, the convention that no type-II error occurs when no alternative is possible. For $\alpha\in(0,1)$ define $$\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r),\alpha)=\inf_{\psi:\,\alpha_\varepsilon(\psi)\le\alpha}\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r),\psi),\qquad \gamma_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r))=\inf_\psi\{\alpha_\varepsilon(\psi)+\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r),\psi)\}.$$ A positive family $r_\varepsilon^*\to0$ is a minimax separation rate if $\gamma_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r_\varepsilon))\to1$ and $\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r_\varepsilon),\alpha)\to1-\alpha$ for every $\alpha\in(0,1)$ whenever $r_\varepsilon/r_\varepsilon^*\to0$, while $\gamma_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r_\varepsilon))\to0$ and $\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r_\varepsilon),\alpha)\to0$ for every $\alpha\in(0,1)$ whenever $r_\varepsilon/r_\varepsilon^*\to\infty$.

references.title: Yuri I. Ingster, Theofanis Sapatinas and Irina A. Suslina, Minimax signal detection in ill-posed inverse problems
Evarist Giné and Richard Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models

items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited from the Gaussian sequence inverse model. The experiment and minimax risks require no additional choice.

items.title: Existence of a finite q=2 ellipsoid extremal profile for small radius
items.statement: Assume the minimax detection-risk definition with $q=2$, and let $a_j$ and $\sigma_j$ be positive nondecreasing sequences tending to infinity. There is a constant $r_0>0$ such that for every $r\in(0,r_0)$ there exist $A,z_0>0$ with finite nonempty $S=\{j:Aa_j^2<1\}$ for which $$\widetilde\eta_j^2=z_0^2\sigma_j^2(1-Aa_j^2)_+$$ satisfies $$\sum_{j\ge1}\sigma_j^2\widetilde\eta_j^2=r^2,\qquad \sum_{j\ge1}a_j^2\sigma_j^2\widetilde\eta_j^2=1.$$

references.title: Yuri I. Ingster, Theofanis Sapatinas and Irina A. Suslina, Minimax signal detection in ill-posed inverse problems, §4.1, Remark 4.1
Evarist Giné and Richard Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models, §6.2.3

items.title: The q=2 ellipsoid extremal profile minimizes the fourth-power objective
items.statement: Assume the minimax detection-risk definition, $q=2$, and positive nondecreasing sequences $a_j$ and $\sigma_j$ with $a_j\to\infty$. Let $A,z_0>0$ and suppose $S=\{j:Aa_j^2<1\}$ is finite and nonempty. Define $\widetilde\eta_j^2=z_0^2\sigma_j^2(1-Aa_j^2)_+$ and assume $$\sum_{j\ge1}\sigma_j^2\widetilde\eta_j^2=r^2,\qquad \sum_{j\ge1}a_j^2\sigma_j^2\widetilde\eta_j^2=1.$$ Then $\widetilde\eta\in\Theta_2(r)$ and minimizes $\sum_{j\ge1}\eta_j^4$ over $\Theta_2(r)$; the nonnegative minimizer is unique.

references.title: Yuri I. Ingster, Theofanis Sapatinas and Irina A. Suslina, Minimax signal detection in ill-posed inverse problems
Clément Marteau and Theofanis Sapatinas, A unified treatment for non-asymptotic and asymptotic approaches to minimax signal detection
Evarist Giné and Richard Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models

items.title: Symmetric Gaussian product-mixture testing bound
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice. In the Gaussian sequence detection experiment, let $v\in\Theta_q(r)$ have finite support $J$ and put $$u(v)^2=\frac{1}{2\varepsilon^4}\sum_{j\in J}v_j^4.$$ Let $\pi_v$ be the uniform probability law on the finite family of mean sequences whose $j$th coordinate is independently $+v_j$ or $-v_j$ for $j\in J$ and is zero off $J$, and let $P_{\pi_v}$ be the corresponding mixture sampling law. Then its likelihood ratio with respect to the null law is $$L_v=\frac{dP_{\pi_v}}{dP_{\varepsilon,0}}=\prod_{j\in J}\exp\!\left(-\frac{v_j^2}{2\varepsilon^2}\right)\cosh\!\left(\frac{v_jY_j}{\varepsilon^2}\right),$$ it satisfies $$\mathbb E_{\varepsilon,0}L_v^2=\prod_{j\in J}\cosh\!\left(\frac{v_j^2}{\varepsilon^2}\right),\qquad \mathbb E_{\varepsilon,0}(L_v-1)^2\le \exp(u(v)^2)-1,$$ and the minimax risks obey $$\gamma_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r))\ge1-\frac12\sqrt{\exp(u(v)^2)-1},\qquad \beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r),\alpha)\ge1-\alpha-\frac12\sqrt{\exp(u(v)^2)-1}$$ for every $\alpha\in(0,1)$.

references.title: Yuri I. Ingster, Theofanis Sapatinas and Irina A. Suslina, Minimax signal detection in ill-posed inverse problems
Evarist Giné and Richard Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models

items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited from the Gaussian sequence inverse model and the change-of-variables supplier. The finite sign prior and likelihood-ratio computations use no additional choice principle.

items.title: q=2 Gaussian-sequence ellipsoid detection boundary
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice and the minimax detection-risk definition with $q=2$. For each $\varepsilon$, suppose $\Theta_2(r_\varepsilon)$ is nonempty and has a finite-support fourth-power minimizer $\widetilde\eta_\varepsilon$ with profile $\widetilde\eta_{\varepsilon,j}^2=z_0^2\sigma_j^2(1-Aa_j^2)_+$ as in the extremal-profile lemma. Put $$u_\varepsilon^2=\frac{1}{2\varepsilon^4}\sum_j\widetilde\eta_{\varepsilon,j}^4,\qquad w_{\varepsilon,j}=\frac{\widetilde\eta_{\varepsilon,j}^2}{\sqrt{2\sum_j\widetilde\eta_{\varepsilon,j}^4}},\qquad w_{\varepsilon,0}=\max_jw_{\varepsilon,j},$$ and define $$T_\varepsilon=\sum_jw_{\varepsilon,j}\bigl((Y_j/\varepsilon)^2-1\bigr),\qquad \psi_{\varepsilon,H}=\mathbf1_{\{T_\varepsilon>H\}}.$$ If $u_\varepsilon\to0$, then $\gamma_\varepsilon(\Theta_2(r_\varepsilon))\to1$ and $\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_2(r_\varepsilon),\alpha)\to1-\alpha$ for every $\alpha\in(0,1)$. If $u_\varepsilon\to\infty$, then for every fixed $c\in(0,1)$ the tests $\psi_{\varepsilon,cu_\varepsilon}$ have total error tending to zero. For the extremal profile, define the finite sums $$J_1=\sum_j\sigma_j^4(1-Aa_j^2)_+,\quad J_2=A\sum_ja_j^2\sigma_j^4(1-Aa_j^2)_+,\quad J_0=\sum_j\sigma_j^4(1-Aa_j^2)_+^2.$$ The active constraints imply $$r_\varepsilon^2=A\frac{J_1}{J_2},\qquad u_\varepsilon^2=\left(\frac{r_\varepsilon}{\varepsilon}\right)^4\frac{J_0}{2J_1^2}.$$

references.title: Yuri I. Ingster, Theofanis Sapatinas and Irina A. Suslina, Minimax signal detection in ill-posed inverse problems
Clément Marteau and Theofanis Sapatinas, A unified treatment for non-asymptotic and asymptotic approaches to minimax signal detection
Evarist Giné and Richard Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models

items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited from the Gaussian sequence inverse model. The two rate-dichotomy branches use only finite likelihood ratios and second-moment bounds; no further choice axiom is used.

items.title: Sparse q<2 detection regime split
items.statement: Assume Countable Choice and the minimax detection-risk definition with $0<q<2$, $a_j=j^\alpha$, $\sigma_j=j^\beta$, and $\alpha,\beta>0$. Let $r_\varepsilon\to0$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, and put $$\lambda=\frac{\alpha+\beta}{2}-\frac{\beta}{q}.$$ For $\lambda>0$, put $A=2\alpha+1/q-1/2$, $B=2(\alpha+\beta)+1/q$, and $D=\alpha+\beta(1-2/q)>0$. Choose any $\delta_\varepsilon>0$ with $\delta_\varepsilon\to0$ and $\delta_\varepsilon\log\varepsilon^{-1}\to\infty$, set $\widetilde r_\varepsilon=r_\varepsilon(1-\delta_\varepsilon)$, and define $$u_\varepsilon^2=2\inf\left\{\sum_{j\ge1}h_j^2\sinh^2(z_j^2/2):\ 0\le h_j\le1,\ z_j\ge0,\ \sum_{j\ge1}j^{2\beta}h_jz_j^2\ge\frac{\widetilde r_\varepsilon^2}{\varepsilon^2},\ \sum_{j\ge1}j^{q(\alpha+\beta)}h_jz_j^q\le\frac1{\varepsilon^q}\right\}.$$ Then the sharp errors have Gaussian form $$\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r_\varepsilon),\alpha)=\Phi(H_\alpha-u_\varepsilon)+o(1),\qquad \gamma_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r_\varepsilon))=2\Phi(-u_\varepsilon/2)+o(1),$$ where $\Phi(t)=(2\pi)^{-1/2}\int_{-\infty}^t e^{-x^2/2}\,dx$ and $H_\alpha$ is its $(1-\alpha)$-quantile. Moreover, $$u_\varepsilon\sim c_{\alpha,\beta,q}\,\varepsilon^{-A/D}r_\varepsilon^{B/D}$$ for a constant $c_{\alpha,\beta,q}>0$, and a minimax separation rate is $$r_\varepsilon^*=\varepsilon^{A/B}.$$ If $\lambda\le0$, put $n_\varepsilon=r_\varepsilon^{-1/\alpha}$ and $D_\varepsilon=n_\varepsilon^{-\beta}r_\varepsilon/\varepsilon-\sqrt{2\log n_\varepsilon}$. Then the sharp errors have degenerate form $$\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r_\varepsilon),\alpha)=(1-\alpha)\Phi(-D_\varepsilon)+o(1),\qquad \gamma_\varepsilon(\Theta_q(r_\varepsilon))=\Phi(-D_\varepsilon)+o(1),$$ and a sharp separation-rate normalization is $$r_\varepsilon^*=\Lambda\,\varepsilon^{\alpha/(\alpha+\beta)}(\log\varepsilon^{-1})^{\alpha/[2(\alpha+\beta)]},\qquad \Lambda=\left(\frac{2}{\alpha+\beta}\right)^{\alpha/[2(\alpha+\beta)]}.$$ Thus the sparse boundary $\lambda=0$ belongs to the degenerate regime, and the two regimes have different separation rates.

references.title: Yuri I. Ingster, Theofanis Sapatinas and Irina A. Suslina, Minimax signal detection in ill-posed inverse problems
Evarist Giné and Richard Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models
Yu. I. Ingster and I. A. Suslina, Nonparametric Goodness-of-Fit Testing Under Gaussian Models, Lecture Notes in Statistics 169, Springer (2003)

items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited from the sequence model and the normal-density change-of-variables supplier. The proved finite-support mixture calculations and the lambda-nonpositive maximum test use no additional choice.

items.title: Sharp Gaussian asymptotics under a vanishing largest weight
items.statement: Assume the $q=2$ ellipsoid detection-boundary theorem, Countable Choice, and the Axiom of Choice. Along a sequence for which $u_\varepsilon$ is bounded above and bounded away from zero and $w_{\varepsilon,0}\to0$, the minimax level-$\alpha$ type-II error and minimax total error satisfy $$\beta_\varepsilon(\Theta_2(r_\varepsilon),\alpha)=\Phi(H_\alpha-u_\varepsilon)+o(1),\qquad \gamma_\varepsilon(\Theta_2(r_\varepsilon))=2\Phi(-u_\varepsilon/2)+o(1),$$ where $\Phi$ is the standard normal distribution function and $H_\alpha$ is defined by $\Phi(H_\alpha)=1-\alpha$. Let $c_{\varepsilon,\alpha}=\inf\{t:\mathbb P_{\varepsilon,0}(T_\varepsilon\le t)\ge1-\alpha\}$; then $\mathbb P_{\varepsilon,0}(T_\varepsilon>c_{\varepsilon,\alpha})\le\alpha$ and $c_{\varepsilon,\alpha}\to H_\alpha$. The weighted tests with thresholds $c_{\varepsilon,\alpha}$ and $u_\varepsilon/2$ attain these asymptotics, while the uncalibrated threshold $H_\alpha$ has asymptotic size $\alpha$. The vanishing-largest-weight condition is required for this Gaussian sharp branch.
items.strategy: Combine the weighted chi-square central limit, a uniform bounded-mean alternative limit, and the local asymptotic normality of the finite symmetric product-mixture likelihood ratio.

references.title: Yuri I. Ingster, Theofanis Sapatinas and Irina A. Suslina, Minimax signal detection in ill-posed inverse problems

Clément Marteau and Theofanis Sapatinas, A unified treatment for non-asymptotic and asymptotic approaches to minimax signal detection

title: Minimax signal detection and separation rates — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: The lambda-zero sparse detection boundary
items.statement: Take $q=1$, $\alpha=\beta=1$, $a_j=j$, and $\sigma_j=j$ in the Gaussian sequence detection experiment. Then the sparse boundary parameter is $\lambda=0$, the source-normalized constant is $\Lambda=1$, and a minimax separation rate has order $$r_\varepsilon^*\asymp\varepsilon^{1/2}(\log\varepsilon^{-1})^{1/4}\qquad(\varepsilon\downarrow0).$$

references.title: Yuri I. Ingster, Theofanis Sapatinas and Irina A. Suslina, Minimax signal detection in ill-posed inverse problems
Yu. I. Ingster and I. A. Suslina, Nonparametric Goodness-of-Fit Testing Under Gaussian Models, Lecture Notes in Statistics 169, Springer (2003)

items.title: Mildly ill-posed Sobolev q=2 detection rate
items.statement: Assume $\alpha,\beta>0$, $q=2$, $a_j=j^\alpha$, and $\sigma_j=j^\beta$ in the Gaussian sequence detection experiment. The minimax separation rate over $\Theta_2(r)$ has order $$r_\varepsilon^*\asymp\varepsilon^{4\alpha/(4\alpha+4\beta+1)}.$$

references.title: Yuri I. Ingster, Theofanis Sapatinas and Irina A. Suslina, Minimax signal detection in ill-posed inverse problems
Evarist Giné and Richard Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models

items.title: Mildly ill-posed analytic q=2 detection rate
items.statement: Assume $\alpha,\beta>0$, $q=2$, $a_j=e^{\alpha j}$, and $\sigma_j=j^\beta$ in the Gaussian sequence detection experiment. The minimax separation rate over $\Theta_2(r)$ has order $$r_\varepsilon^*\asymp\varepsilon(\log\varepsilon^{-1})^{\beta+1/4}.$$

references.title: Yuri I. Ingster, Theofanis Sapatinas and Irina A. Suslina, Minimax signal detection in ill-posed inverse problems
Evarist Giné and Richard Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models

items.title: Severely ill-posed Sobolev q=2 detection rate
items.statement: Assume $\alpha,\beta>0$, $q=2$, $a_j=j^\alpha$, and $\sigma_j=e^{\beta j}$ in the Gaussian sequence detection experiment. A minimax separation rate over $\Theta_2(r)$ is $$r_\varepsilon^*\asymp\left(\frac{\log\varepsilon^{-1}}{\beta}\right)^{-\alpha}.$$

references.title: Yuri I. Ingster, Theofanis Sapatinas and Irina A. Suslina, Minimax signal detection in ill-posed inverse problems
Evarist Giné and Richard Nickl, Mathematical Foundations of Infinite-Dimensional Statistical Models

items.title: Severely ill-posed analytic q=2 detection rate
items.statement: Assume $\alpha,\beta>0$, $q=2$, $a_j=e^{\alpha j}$, and $\sigma_j=e^{\beta j}$ in the Gaussian sequence detection experiment. A minimax separation rate over $\Theta_2(r)$ is $$r_\varepsilon^*\asymp\varepsilon^{\alpha/(\alpha+\beta)}.$$

references.title: Yuri I. Ingster, Theofanis Sapatinas and Irina A. Suslina, Minimax signal detection in ill-posed inverse problems
